answer.read: Blankstahl opened at a price above today's level with no clause, pay 30 d, 12 months (offer:70740-0). It cites index rises to justify that, but the recent AS-14404 move is down (a1) and so is PPI-C2431 (a4). It said it is focusing on customers with volume (Z, M5), so a longer, steady commitment matters to it. Its owner offered to open its calculation (M1), which suggests some price flexibility. Price moves above two percent need its pricing committee (M3), so concessions will come slowly. It is financially stable (credit index flat) and wants a clause (Z, 09-22). The clause options cost us more, though.
answer.message: Thank you for your offer. The indices you cite have eased recently, and our recent orders for this part were placed at a level well below your quote, so we cannot accept a price increase. We propose a longer commitment with fixed pricing and no adjustment clause, as set out in the attached sheet. We are also open to going through your calculation together if that helps settle the price.
answer.reason: o5 and o6 have the lowest C (€232,559), and pay 45 d gives the supplier slightly better cash than the engine's 60–90 d terms. The 36-month term in o6 answers its stated focus on volume customers without costing us anything in C. E0 is about €175 worse on C. The clause options cost us more and give up the index downside we can currently cite. The deep anchor is a first counter, and the committee process means it will move in steps. a1, a4 and a5 directly rebut the price rise it is asking for. We left out the delivery record (a2) and the small forecast increase (a3) because they are weaker points.
